title: Probabilistic Cycle Capacity Simulator and "What-if" Planner for Staffing Decisions
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Problem: Current cycle staffing decisions are largely deterministic (headcount * assumed velocity) and don’t capture uncertainty from attrition, unplanned incidents, cross-team dependencies, or variability in task size. This leads to conservative buffers or reactive mid-cycle scope cuts.

Goal: Deliver a probabilistic cycle capacity model + interactive 'what-if' planner that helps PMs and ENG leads simulate multiple scenarios (attrition, incident week, parallel initiatives) and surface recommended commitment bands (conservative/likely/aggressive) with suggested scope trims or backfill actions.

Scope:
- Build a backend estimator that ingests team rosters, skill availability, historical throughput distributions, and active dependencies and produces a Monte Carlo distribution of cycle throughput.
- Expose a lightweight web UI in Console (mock wireframe) to run scenarios: reduce FTE by X%, add urgent incident requiring Y person-weeks, reassign N engineers for a week, enable emergency hire/backfill.
- Produce actionable outputs: 3 commitment bands (90% safe, 70% likely, 50% stretch), expected delivery dates for each initiative, recommended scope candidates to move to backlog based on dev effort and dependency cost.
- Integration: optional CSV import and link to cycle roster in HR view; export results as PNG/CSV for leadership.

Out of scope for MVP: automated hiring actions, live sync to payroll/HR, full fidelity task-level simulation (we’ll approximate by zone-level effort buckets).
acceptance_criteria: Estimator returns throughput distribution (percentiles 10/25/50/75/90) within 10s for typical team sizes (<=40 engineers).
UI allows PM to run at least 4 scenario types and compare output bands side-by-side.
Generated recommendation includes at least one scope-trim candidate per initiative when conservative band fails to meet committed stories.
Exported CSV includes inputs, sampled outcomes, and chosen band metadata.
Demo with 3 cross-functional teams (runtime, console, infra) completed and feedback captured.
Documentation and a short runbook for interpreting bands attached to ticket links.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Marisol Vega: Kickoff with Eng leads. Agreed on Monte Carlo approach rather than analytic approximation; historical throughput distributions are available from our internal cadence dashboard. Next: engineering spike to time performance and memory profile.

2026-03-02 - Ben Liu (Eng): Ran quick spike on sampling approach. For team sizes up to 40, 10k Monte Carlo iterations takes ~7s in Go runtime when we pre-aggregate task-size distribution. Memory ~120MB. We can meet the <10s goal if we reuse sampled kernels and cache results per-roster snapshot.

2026-03-04 - Design (Camila Ortega): Wireframes for scenario UI attached (link: drive/redwood/capacity-sim/wireframe-v1). Focused on clear band visualizations and export button. Keep language non-technical for PM audience (avoid 'p-value' jargon).

2026-03-06 - Liam Patel: Requested ability to mark certain engineers as 'non-replaceable' (critical path owners) so simulator treats their unavailability as higher impact. Added as a small scope change — include in MVP toggle.

2026-03-10 - Security (Anika Rao): Flagged data sensitivity: roster-level skill tags may be PII-adjacent. We need to ensure CSV imports and exports scrub employee IDs and only use role/skill buckets. Marking security_review_required=true and adding to dependencies.

2026-03-12 - Marisol Vega: Demo scheduled for 2026-03-25 with PM guild and Eng leads. Action items: complete backend prototype, basic UI, privacy scrub, and two scenario templates (attrition and incident-week).
